doc: Dither: quantise to `levels` values per channel (0 and 1 included) with 'ordered' Bayer dithering (matrix 2, 4 or 8, tiled on the document origin) or 'diffusion'. colour=false quantises the luma and outputs grey. strength mixes the dithered result with the original. Alpha unchanged. 'diffusion' is a WINDOWED Floyd-Steinberg (7,3,5,1)/16 error diffusion: true error diffusion is sequential over the whole image (each pixel depends on all previous ones), which a GPU cannot do and which would make a region render depend on the whole document. Instead every pixel re-simulates the algorithm in integer arithmetic (8-bit straight colour * 16, floor shifts) over the causal window of rows y-6..y and columns x-12..x+6 (left to right, no serpentine, the error entering the window from its top row and left column is a pseudo-random value in +-half a step hashed from the document position, because otherwise every pixel of a flat area would simulate the same window and get the same value) and outputs the result for its own position. The error propagation is therefore truncated to 6 rows / ~12 columns: it is an approximation of true error diffusion (same look and local tone reproduction, but not bit-identical to a sequential run, and the pattern differs slightly near where the window starts), exactly reproducible on every GPU because no float accumulation is involved.

matrix.doc: Bayer matrix size, 2 | 4 | 8 (3 -> 4, 5..7 -> 8); ordered mode only
